title: Strict functoriality of the contravariant Grothendieck comma retraction
statement:
Use small ordinary categories and nerves as in [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. For a small category $C$ and a strict functor $F:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ with small values, define $A_F$ with objects $(c,a)$, $a\in F(c)$, and arrows $(h,u):(c,a)\to(d,b)$, where $h:c\to d$ and $u:a\to F(h)b$. Composition is $(k,v)(h,u)=(kh,F(h)(v)u)$. Let $P_F:A_F\to C$ be projection. Define $D_F(c)=(c\downarrow P_F)$ with objects $(x,t:c\to P_Fx)$ and arrows $v:(x,t)\to(y,t')$ satisfying $P_F(v)t=t'$, with precomposition in $t$ as its contravariant action. Define the functor $R^F_c:D_F(c)\to F(c)$ by $R^F_c((d,a),t)=F(t)a$ and $R^F_c((h,u))=F(t)u$.

For small $C'$, $F':C'^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$, a functor $H:C'\to C$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:F'\Rightarrow F H^{\mathrm{op}}$, the formulas
$$K(c',a')=(Hc',\alpha_{c'}a'),\qquad K(h',u')=(Hh',\alpha_{c'}(u'))$$
define a functor $K:A_{F'}\to A_F$ with $P_FK=HP_{F'}$. The functors
$$L_{c'}:D_{F'}(c')\to D_F(Hc'),\quad (x',t')\mapsto(Kx',Ht'),\quad v'\mapsto Kv'$$
commute strictly with precomposition in $c'$ and satisfy the equality of functors $R^F_{Hc'}L_{c'}=\alpha_{c'}R^{F'}_{c'}$.

These assignments preserve identity data and composition strictly: for $J:C''\to C'$ and $\gamma:F''\Rightarrow F'J^{\mathrm{op}}$, put $\delta_{c''}=\alpha_{Jc''}\gamma_{c''}$. Then $K_{HJ,\delta}=K_{H,\alpha}K_{J,\gamma}$ and $L^{HJ,\delta}_{c''}=L^{H,\alpha}_{Jc''}L^{J,\gamma}_{c''}$, and identity data induce identity functors. No component of $\alpha$ and no functor $H$ is required to be an equivalence.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, 9.1 and 9.10, printed pp.31–33: the first comma retraction in Lemma 9.7, with simultaneous base/contravariant-endpoint functoriality. No Stacks tag states this categorical bar calculation; source formulas checked online, agent expansion of strict naturality.

proof.text: The formulas in the statement really define $A_F$. Its identity at $(c,a)$ is $(1_c,1_a)$. For three successive arrows $(h,u),(k,v),(\ell,w)$, the two bracketings have base $\ell kh$ and the same fibre arrow $F(h)F(k)(w)\,F(h)(v)\,u$: use $F(kh)=F(h)F(k)$ and preservation of composition by $F(h)$. The unit laws follow from $F(1_c)=1_{F(c)}$. Projection to the base therefore defines $P_F$. In $D_F(c)$, composing $v:(x,t)\to(y,t')$ and $w:(y,t')\to(z,t'')$ is permitted because $P_F(wv)t=P_F(w)P_F(v)t=P_F(w)t'=t''$. Identities also satisfy the triangle equation. For $s:b\to c$, precomposition sends $(x,t)$ to $(x,ts)$ and leaves $v$ unchanged; the triangle equation becomes $P_F(v)ts=t's$. Associativity and units in $C$ give $D_F(s)D_F(r)=D_F(rs)$ for $r:c\to d$, and $D_F(1)=1$. All these verifications also apply to $F'$ and $F''$.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, 9.1 and 9.10 (printed pp.31–32): explicit strict naturality expansion, calculation 1.

proof.text:
Check the stated $R^F_c$ on arrows, not just objects. An arrow represented by $(h,u):(d,a)\to(e,b)$ has $ht=t'$, so $F(t)u$ ends at $F(t)F(h)b=F(t')b$. On a consecutive arrow $(k,v)$ its value on the composite is
$$F(t)(F(h)(v)u)=F(ht)(v)\,F(t)(u),$$
which is the composite of the two $R^F_c$ images. It sends identities to identities. Thus $R^F_c$ is a functor. Moreover, for $s:b\to c$, on an object and on a fibre arrow $u$ the formulas $F(ts)a=F(s)F(t)a$ and $F(ts)u=F(s)F(t)u$ show the strict equality $R^F_bD_F(s)=F(s)R^F_c$.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, 9.1 and 9.10 (printed pp.31–32): explicit strict naturality expansion, calculation 2.

proof.text:
Write $h':c'\to d'$. Naturality of $\alpha$ is the equality of functors
$$\alpha_{c'}F'(h')=F(Hh')\alpha_{d'}.$$
Consequently $\alpha_{c'}u'$ has target $\alpha_{c'}F'(h')b'=F(Hh')\alpha_{d'}b'$, so $K(h',u')$ has exactly the required type. For a consecutive $(k',v')$, functoriality of $\alpha_{c'}$ and the displayed naturality equality on the arrow $v'$ give
$$\alpha_{c'}(F'(h')(v')u')=F(Hh')(\alpha_{d'}v')\,\alpha_{c'}u'.$$
Together with $H(k'h')=Hk'\,Hh'$, this is $K((k',v')(h',u'))=K(k',v')K(h',u')$. Functors $H$ and $\alpha_{c'}$ preserve identities, giving the identity law. On $(c',a')$ and $(h',u')$, the two projection composites give respectively $Hc'$ and $Hh'$. Thus $P_FK=HP_{F'}$ strictly.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, 9.1 and 9.10 (printed pp.31–32): explicit strict naturality expansion, calculation 3.

proof.text:
For a comma arrow $v':(x',t')\to(y',t'')$ in $D_{F'}(c')$, the proposed image satisfies
$$P_F(Kv')\,Ht'=H(P_{F'}v')\,Ht'=H(P_{F'}(v')t')=Ht''.$$
Hence $L_{c'}$ is defined on arrows. Its identity and composition laws follow directly from those of $K$, since comma composition is the underlying composition. For $s':b'\to c'$, both $L_{b'}D_{F'}(s')$ and $D_F(Hs')L_{c'}$ send $(x',t')$ to $(Kx',H(t's'))=(Kx',(Ht')(Hs'))$ and send $v'$ to $Kv'$. This proves the asserted strict commutation with precomposition.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, 9.1 and 9.10 (printed pp.31–32): explicit strict naturality expansion, calculation 4.

proof.text:
Let $x'=(d',a')$ and $t':c'\to d'$. The object images in the retraction square are equal, since naturality at $t'$ gives
$$R^F_{Hc'}L_{c'}(x',t')=F(Ht')\alpha_{d'}a'=\alpha_{c'}F'(t')a'=\alpha_{c'}R^{F'}_{c'}(x',t').$$
For an arrow $v'=(h',u'):(x',t')\to(y',t'')$, with $h't'=t''$, the left composite has arrow image $F(Ht')(\alpha_{d'}u')$, and the right one has image $\alpha_{c'}(F'(t')u')$. The same naturality equality, now evaluated on $u'$, makes them equal. Their targets agree by $h't'=t''$ and Step 2. Equality on objects and arrows proves equality of functors, rather than just an isomorphism.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, 9.1 and 9.10 (printed pp.31–32): explicit strict naturality expansion, calculation 5.

proof.text:
For the composable data in the statement, the family $\delta_{c''}=\alpha_{Jc''}\gamma_{c''}$ is natural: for $s'':c''\to d''$, naturality of $\gamma$ and then of $\alpha$ gives
$$\alpha_{Jc''}\gamma_{c''}F''(s'')=\alpha_{Jc''}F'(Js'')\gamma_{d''}=F(HJs'')\alpha_{Jd''}\gamma_{d''}.$$
On $(c'',a'')$, both $K_{HJ,\delta}$ and $K_{H,\alpha}K_{J,\gamma}$ have image $(HJc'',\alpha_{Jc''}\gamma_{c''}a'')$. On $(h'',u'')$ both have image $(HJh'',\alpha_{Jc''}(\gamma_{c''}u''))$. This proves their strict equality.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, 9.1 and 9.10 (printed pp.31–32): explicit strict naturality expansion, calculation 6.

proof.text: On $(x'',t'')\in D_{F''}(c'')$, the composite $L^{H,\alpha}_{Jc''}L^{J,\gamma}_{c''}$ has image $(K_{H,\alpha}K_{J,\gamma}x'',H(Jt''))$. Step 6 identifies this with $(K_{HJ,\delta}x'',(HJ)t'')$, the image under $L^{HJ,\delta}_{c''}$. On arrows both images are $K_{HJ,\delta}v''$ by the same step. For identity data $(1_C,1_F)$, the $K$ formulas give $(c,a)\mapsto(c,a)$ and $(h,u)\mapsto(h,u)$; the $L$ formulas give $(x,t)\mapsto(x,t)$ and $v\mapsto v$. They are therefore identity functors. Every equality used only functor laws and naturality, so no equivalence condition on any component or on a base functor has entered.
